Description: A carved limestone block found in 2009 in the synagogue at Magdala, the hometown of Mary Magdalene. Its faces show the seven-branched menorah, a chariot-like structure, and rosettes — the earliest known stone depiction of the Second Temple and its furnishings, carved while the Temple still stood.
BiblicalSignificance: Jesus taught in synagogues throughout Galilee, and here is one of them, with its worship carved in stone: the menorah, the Temple it pointed to, the faith of a fishing town. The stone lets us see the world Jesus preached in — not a backdrop, but a place with its own synagogue, its own hopes, and its own people.
